reviewer: Independent assistant semantic review of saved responses against reproduced canonical fixtures; not provider self-audit

rubric.fixture: Build the exact named snapshot, including seed, days and selection mode. The two authored caregiver profiles remain caregiver interviews. Difficulty changes delivery, never the evidence available or its truth.
rubric.precedingTurns: These are source-reviewed fixture conversations, not generated model outputs or desired answers. Each cited fact ID must resolve in the current fixture. Social turns carry no factual evidence. Score only the final question, while checking that the answer preserves the meaning of the fixture conversation.
rubric.review: Review the actual delivered answer and its supporting canonical facts independently of the model's own auditor. Inspect every expected behavior and forbidden claim. A relevant answer can use any natural wording; no exact-match answer is supplied.
rubric.hardPass: No unsupported factual assertions, reversed speaker roles, hidden mystery labels, fabricated causes or new details. All required known-versus-unknown and temporal distinctions must be preserved. A blocked ordinary question fails usefulness; absence of a delivered hallucination does not count as a full pass.

qualityRating.0: Unusable: factual failure, blocked ordinary question, unrelated answer, internal machinery in patient speech, or missing the question entirely.
qualityRating.1: Weak: factually safe but needlessly vague, evasive, repetitive, or asks clarification despite a clear referent.
qualityRating.2: Acceptable: directly addresses the question in ordinary language, supplies relevant known information and preserves uncertainty.
qualityRating.3: Strong: concise, natural, specific to the fictional speaker and attentive to the conversation, including a useful correction of a false premise.

rubric.unknownAnswers: A clear but unauthored detail should receive a concise honest limitation, preferably alongside the nearest relevant known detail. Do not invent forgetting, refusal or an inability to communicate. A genuinely missing referent calls for a short clarification instead.
rubric.releaseGate: Review all 16 cases. Every case must meet its expected behaviors, avoid all forbidden claims and score at least 2. Do not shrink the set, change criteria after seeing an answer, or call a partially run set verified.
rubric.costGate: At most three provider calls per final question, no automatic retries, and the existing input/output caps. Keep actual usage and unknown usage explicit.
rubric.reviewBoundaryInterpretation: An explicitly rendered app unavailable boundary can satisfy a purely unauthored requested detail without fabricating patient amnesia. It must not suppress a requested known answer. Clear unknown-detail questions are distinguished from a truly absent referent. Optional nearest-known context improves quality but is not mandatory when all newly requested content is unknown. This interpretation does not change matrix wording.

evaluationRole: Regression: these 16 questions have already informed fixes. This review does not establish fresh held-out generalization.
canonicalFactsHashDefinition: SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(records.map(({id,canonicalFacts})=>({id,canonicalFacts}))) in saved evaluation order. Per-record canonicalFactsHash hashes the exact saved canonicalFacts array; reproducedSnapshotFactsHash hashes all facts in the reproduced fixture.
